title: Actor Chad Lowe's 13-Year-Old Daughter Died by Suicide, Medical Examiner Says
text:
report.
The medical examiner’s report, case No. 2026-15453, lists Fiona Lowe as a White female whose place of death was a hospital. The report lists the manner of death as suicide and the cause of death as hanging. The case remained open, and her body was listed as ready for release.
Lowe and his wife, Kim Painter, announced their daughter’s death in a statement shared with People on Tuesday.
The family said it was “deeply heartbroken” by the loss of Fiona, who was 13.
“She was adored by her sisters and she was deeply loved by her parents. In fact, she was the light of our lives,” the family said in the statement. “Her passing is devastating for our entire family and we ask for prayers and privacy at this time.”
The family did not publicly disclose Fiona’s cause of death in its statement. It included a message directing people experiencing mental health struggles to seek help.
“If you or someone you know is struggling with mental health, please reach out to the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline by calling or texting 988,” the family said.
Fiona was born Nov. 15, 2012. She was the middle child of Lowe and Painter, who married in 2010.
The couple’s oldest daughter, Mabel, is 17 and was born in May 2009. Their youngest daughter, Nixie, is 10 and was born in March 2016.
Lowe marked Fiona’s 13th birthday with an Instagram post in November. He shared a photo of his daughter and wrote: “Celebrating Fiona officially becoming a teen today!! Keep dancing through life FiBear! Love you soooo much!”
The post later drew messages of sympathy from followers. One commenter wrote: “As a parent, I can't even imagine the pain.” Another wrote: “Sending prayers for the entire family.”
Celebrities also shared public condolences after the family announced Fiona’s death.
wroteon X. “Fly high, Fiona Lowe. Love you Chad and Kim.”
Actor Cary Elwes also paid respect for the family in an Instagram post. Elwes appeared with Chad Lowe and his brother, Rob Lowe, in the 1984 film “Oxford Blues.”
“Our hearts are broken for you all,” Elwes wrote. “Thinking of you and praying for you. Always.”
Chad Lowe is known for his role as Jesse McKenna on ABC’s “Life Goes On,” which earned him a Primetime Emmy Award in 1993. His other work includes “Unfaithful,” “Pretty Little Liars,” “Melrose Place,” “ER,” “24,” “Supergirl” and “9-1-1: Lone Star.”
